data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference smuggles in induction because selecting a theory for future action based on past test survival logically presupposes that past performance is a reliable guide to future reliability, which is the definition of the inductive principle Popper sought to eliminate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the preference can be shown to rely purely on the logical status of currently unfalsified theories without reference to future expectations.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'preference' is redefined as mere 'temporary retention' without any implication of superior fitness for future tasks.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the cost of abandoning the preference is shown to be total scientific paralysis, forcing a pragmatic rather than logical justification.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Hidden Inductive Leap: The act of 'preferring' implies an expectation of future utility or truth-likeness derived from past data, which cannot be justified deductively and thus re-introduces the very problem Popper claimed to solve.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
